units.translation: where, having heard the chorus's ὠγμῷ [cry of lament], which is marked by the stage direction ὠγμός [a cry of lament], Clytaemnestra asks: Schol. ὡς παρὰ τὸ αἴ αἴ αἰάζειν, οὕτω παρὰ τὸ ὦ ὤ ὤζειν [just as from αἴ αἴ [alas, alas] comes αἰάζειν [to cry alas], so from ὦ ὤ [oh, oh] comes ὤζειν [to cry oh]]. For examples of others see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2000.
Are you crying out? Are you sleeping?
stage direction: a cry of lament
just as from αἴ αἴ [alas, alas] comes αἰάζειν [to cry alas], so from ὦ ὤ [oh, oh] comes ὤζειν [to cry oh]
oh! (exclamation of one shouting or calling)
an exclamation of one shouting or calling
It is not found in Sophocles nor in the comic poets, but several times in Euripides: see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2000.
You would be sleeping, oh! and what need is there of sleeping women?
to thrust me out of the house and fatherland.
For you will never say that a friend of Oceanus is more steadfast to you.
the unquenchable stream from father Oceanus.
and the bronze-thundering lake by Oceanus.
Schol. τὴν ὀξέως μετελθοῦσαν αὐτόν [the one who swiftly pursued him].
For I speak of an ancient transgression, swift in punishment.
the one who swiftly pursued him
having come to my father at the swift-passing ferry of sorrows.
ships like swift-winged ones have come.
and take the swiftest opportunity of these things.
this arm is fitted hard to loosen.
Olenus: a city of Achaea and Aetolia, spoken of in the feminine gender.
"steep and sacred Olenus" (the Paris codex adds τ᾽ [and]).
I shudder at the house-destroying goddess.
a cruel-biting desire urges you too much.
Of girls whose virginity was taken by enemies, where the scholium says: ὑπὸ τῶν ὠμῶς αὐτῶν δρεπομένων τὴν ήβην πρὸ τῶν νομίμων γάμων [by those who cruelly pluck their youth before lawful marriage].
before the lawful rites of unripe-plucked maidens.
by those who cruelly pluck their youth before lawful marriage
resting on his shoulders (thus from the copy for ὤμοις [shoulders]) the pillar of heaven and earth.
Thus Klausen for αιωμαναιρειν. ἔριν [to take away strife]. Hermann had restored ἔριν [strife] from the scholiast's note, and wrote διώκειν ἔριν [to pursue strife].
a cruel spirit, not named after maidens.
and cruel in all things to slaves and beyond measure.
how with cruel mind the deity entered the race of the Persians.
where Turnebus reads ὠνοῖτο [he might buy]. M has ὤνοιτο, as if he had intended ὄνοιτο [he might blame], which Boissonade conjectured.
who would buy friends who are already owned?
the time of blooming age, youthful age, the flower of youth
and it is time for merchants to let down the anchor (I corrected καθιέναι [to let down]).
and they sacrificed night-honored meals on the hearth of fire, a season shared by none of the gods.
